summary.headline: Poultry profits have recovered strongly, but the price already assumes the good part of the cycle lasts
summary.text: Bairaha Farms PLC (BFL.N0000) is one of Sri Lanka's oldest integrated poultry businesses: breeder farms, hatcheries, broilers, processing and value-added chicken, with 50% joint ventures in a feed mill and a grandparent farm. After a poor 2024/25 (profit Rs 122mn), 2025/26 profit jumped to Rs 1,001mn and April–September 2026 profit rose 13% to Rs 456mn on higher chick and chicken prices. But Rs 400mn of 2025/26 profit was a non-cash gain on revaluing breeder birds, the joint ventures have swung to losses on corn import limits, and return on equity has averaged only about 9–10% over the cycle. Once the breeder flock is replaced each year, little cash is left after capex. Six methods at a 14.7% required return give a fair value of **Rs 63.44**. At Rs 86.90 (30 September 2026 close) the share is about 37% above that. Buy price Rs 53.92; strong buy Rs 47.58. It passes two of the four business tests (debt and cash), so it is in category 3 (avoid for now).

quality.reason: Debt is modest and profit turns into cash, but return on equity has been under 15% in most years and profit swings with chick and feed prices; 40% of 2025/26 profit was a non-cash breeder-bird valuation gain.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more

modelsNote: All six methods are averaged equally. Growth check: assumed 3% / 7% / 10% against a supported 11.9% (reinvestment rate 104% × return on capital 11.5%, 2025/26), all within the limit. The DCF covers the poultry business only (the cash flow excludes the joint ventures, whose dividends sit in investing) and takes off the breeder birds bought each year (Rs 1.19bn over the twelve months) as a running cost; the joint ventures are added at 0.6× / 0.9× / 1.1× book. NOPAT excludes the Rs 400mn bird fair value gain and uses 30% tax. Maintenance capex Rs 0.70 / 0.50 / 0.40bn: the calculator's range (1.24 / 0.81 / 0.37) is pushed up by the 2025/26 growth projects. Cost of debt 8.2% (interest paid ÷ average borrowings, 2025/26) is just over 4 points under the bond yield because the Islamic financing is short-term and priced off AWPLR, which fell during 2025/26 (CFO's review, p. 24).

higher: Full-year 2026/27 EPS above Rs 11 with no bird revaluation gain.
The joint-venture feed mill back to steady profit (corn imports allowed again) and paying dividends.
The Kurunegala farm and hatchery expansion lifting return on equity to 15%+ through a weaker chick-price year.
A higher, steady payout (over 30%) funded from operating cash.
lower: Chick or chicken prices falling back as in 2024/25 (industry oversupply).
Feed-mill losses continuing, or a call on the Rs 3.36bn of guarantees for its bank loans.
Another disease outbreak (avian influenza) or cyclone hitting the breeder farms.
Capex continuing to be funded by short-term borrowing.

fullText:
**Summary**

Bairaha Farms PLC (BFL.N0000), founded in 1975, is an integrated poultry business: breeder farms, hatcheries selling day-old chicks, broiler farming (own and out-grower), processing of whole chicken and portions, and value-added products (sausages, cold cuts, pre-cooked meat through Bairaha Foods). It owns 50% of Fortune Agro Industries (a feed mill) and Fortune G-P Farms (grandparent birds), which are equity-accounted. The founding family's executive directors hold about 36%.

Poultry is cyclical. In 2024/25 an industry glut of chicks and chicken cut profit to Rs 122mn. In 2025/26 prices recovered (chicks +25%, chicken +7%) and profit rose to Rs 1,001mn (EPS Rs 11.71), and April–September 2026 profit rose 13% to Rs 456mn. But Rs 400mn of 2025/26 profit was a non-cash gain on revaluing breeder birds, Rs 351mn came from the joint ventures (now loss-making), and over six years return on equity has averaged only about 9–10%.

My fair value is **Rs 63.44**. Buy price **Rs 53.92** (fair value less 15%), strong buy **Rs 47.58** (less 25%). At Rs 86.90 (close on 30 September 2026; the current CSE price wasn't available to this run) the share is about 37% above fair value. It passes two of the four business tests (debt and cash) and fails returns and steady profit: **category 3, avoid for now**.

**Latest results**

| | Apr–Sep 2026 | Apr–Sep 2025 | 2025/26 | 2024/25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Rs 8,576mn | Rs 7,689mn | Rs 15,291mn | Rs 13,916mn |
| Gross margin | 21.4% | 18.0% | 18.9% | 12.5% |
| Operating profit (before JVs) | Rs 851mn | Rs 545mn | Rs 1,082mn | Rs 105mn |
| Share of joint ventures | −Rs 59mn | −Rs 12mn | Rs 351mn | Rs 286mn |
| Profit attributable | Rs 463mn | Rs 407mn | Rs 1,031mn | Rs 125mn |
| EPS | Rs 5.27 | Rs 4.63 | Rs 11.71 | Rs 1.42 |

- 2025/26 operating profit includes a Rs 400mn fair value gain on breeder birds (Rs 13mn in 2024/25). It is non-cash and reverses if chick prices fall.
- Tax is now a full 30%: in April–September 2025 old tax losses kept tax to Rs 45mn; this year it was Rs 226mn.
- The September quarter was weaker: profit before joint ventures −4% and a Rs 75mn joint-venture loss, because the feed mill could import only 20% of its approved corn and the corn levy doubled to Rs 50/kg (MD's comment).
- Shares were split 1:5 in December 2025; there are 88mn shares. All per-share figures here are on today's shares unless marked.

**The cash question**

Bairaha must replace its breeder (parent) flock every year: it bought Rs 1,162mn of birds in 2025/26 and Rs 1,055mn in 2024/25. The annual cash flow statement shows these purchases under investing and adds the birds used back into operating cash, so headline operating cash (Rs 1.92bn) overstates what the business really generates. After bird purchases, operating cash was Rs 762mn in 2025/26 and Rs 967mn in the twelve months to September 2026. PPE capex was Rs 1.23bn in 2025/26 (mostly growth: the Kurunegala broiler farm, hatchery, a USD 1mn cold store) and Rs 582mn in April–September 2026, so free cash has been negative and the gap was borrowed. Net debt is moderate at Rs 2.26bn (0.31× equity), but Bairaha also guarantees Rs 3.36bn of the feed-mill joint venture's bank loans.

**Valuation**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF of the poultry business + joint ventures | 9.82 | 52.12 | 106.71 | 50.35 |
| P/E (justified, EPS to March 2027) | 36.89 | 66.61 | 108.51 | 66.07 |
| Justified price to book | 40.56 | 68.02 | 114.56 | 69.09 |
| Residual income | 32.43 | 61.40 | 122.42 | 64.91 |
| Dividends (two-stage) | 26.55 | 53.04 | 98.11 | 54.11 |
| NAV (adjusted) | 69.06 | 76.74 | 85.04 | 76.10 |
| **Average** | **35.89** | **62.99** | **105.89** | **63.44** |

Weights bear 30 / base 50 / bull 20. Cost of equity 14.7% (beta 0.63, provisional), WACC 12.9%.

- **DCF.** Start: twelve-month cash before interest Rs 2.35bn, less breeder birds Rs 1.19bn, less maintenance capex Rs 0.70 / 0.50 / 0.40bn = Rs 0.46 / 0.66 / 0.76bn. NOPAT Rs 691mn (twelve-month operating profit Rs 1,387mn less the bird gain, at 30% tax). Growth 3% / 7% / 10% for five years, then 4% / 5% / 6%, reinvesting growth ÷ 9% / 12% / 14% return on capital; less net debt Rs 2.26bn. The poultry business alone is worth −Rs 5.5 / 29.1 / 78.6 a share; the joint ventures add Rs 15.3 / 23.0 / 28.1 (0.6× / 0.9× / 1.1× book). In the base and bull cases 78% and 86% of the DCF value comes after year 5, so the result leans on the long run. Returns on new capital close to WACC mean growth adds little value.
- **P/E.** EPS to March 2027 Rs 7.50 / 10.50 / 12.50 × justified P/E 4.9× / 6.3× / 8.7× (payout 1 − g ÷ ROE at long-run ROE 10% / 13% / 16%). Base EPS is 15% below the Rs 12.35 twelve-month run-rate because that includes the bird gain (about Rs 3.2 a share after tax) and low tax; it matches April–September 2026 annualised (Rs 10.54).
- **P/B and residual income.** Book Rs 82.48. ROE of 10% / 13% / 16% against a 16.2% / 14.7% / 13.2% required return: only the bull case earns more than the cost of equity.
- **Dividends.** Rs 1.80 next year, growing 3% / 7% / 10%, then the payout rises to 1 − g ÷ ROE. The current payout (16%) is low because capex comes first.
- **NAV.** Rs 82.48 less the after-tax bird revaluation (Rs 3.2) and a 40% / 10% / 0% discount on the joint ventures (bull adds 10%).

Growth check: assumed 3% / 7% / 10%; supported 11.9% (2025/26 reinvestment 104% of NOPAT × 11.5% return on capital). All scenarios are within it, and the bull case's 10% needs the new farm and hatchery to run full.

**What the price implies**

At Rs 86.90 the market pays 1.05× book and 8.3× base EPS. At a 14.7% required return that needs a long-run ROE of about 16%, a level Bairaha reached only in 2021/22 and 2025/26, both peak-price years.

**Business tests**

- Return on equity 15%+: **fail** (16% now with the bird gain, about 11% without; 9–10% over six years).
- Net debt no more than equity: **pass** (0.31×; but Rs 3.36bn of joint-venture guarantees).
- Steady profit: **fail** (no loss since 2019/20, but profit swung from Rs 1,001mn to Rs 122mn and back; 2025/26 relied on the bird gain and joint ventures).
- Profit turns into cash: **pass** (operating cash after bird purchases exceeded profit over two years).

Two passes: weak, **category 3 (avoid for now)**.

**Buy plan (500 shares)**

| Tranche | Shares | Up to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 | Rs 53.92 |
| 2 | 150 | Rs 50.75 |
| 3 | 150 | Rs 47.58 |

Average about Rs 51.07, Rs 25,534 in total. Rs 53.92 needs a 38% fall. Since the split the share has traded at Rs 66.50–95.90; in the 2024/25 glut it reached Rs 150 before the split (Rs 30 today), so the buy price is plausible only in a poultry downturn. Given the weak business tests, wait for a downturn and a year of steady joint-venture profit.

**Management and plans**

The CFO targets about 20% revenue growth in 2026/27 with margin recovery from new capacity, and lower gearing. First-half revenue grew 11.5%, margins improved and net debt was flat, but the joint ventures, which management expected to keep improving, lost Rs 59mn.

**What would change my view**

Higher: 2026/27 EPS above Rs 11 without bird gains; the feed mill back in steady profit; ROE of 15%+ through a weaker price year; a higher payout funded from operating cash.

Lower: chick or chicken prices falling back; continued feed-mill losses or a call on the guarantees; avian influenza or another cyclone; more capex funded with short-term debt.

**Uncertain or missing**

- The share price is the 30 September 2026 close; the current CSE price couldn't be fetched.
- The beta is provisional (Damodaran's global sector betas as stand-ins; no local 5-year betas reachable).
- Interim cash flows show breeder-bird purchases net of birds used, while the annual one shows them gross; the twelve-month figure combines the two, which gives the same cash after birds but should be checked against the next annual report.
- The interim reports don't say whether any breeder-bird fair value change is in the half-year profit.
- 2020/21–2023/24 figures come only from the ten-year summary.
